page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-32 is a memory-dense virtual machine configuration featuring 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated Intel Xeon physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Supporting symmetric multithreading with two threads per core, the system includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The instance delivers 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It includes no bundled local storage and features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on attached network storage and configured cloud networking interfaces. The architecture also operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate middle-tier computational and memory throughput across standard enterprise evaluations. The instance recorded a multi-core stress-ng score of 30,097.54 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,454.0, complemented by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 107.01 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 47.28 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput attained 26.96 million operations per second, while PassMark database operations reached 11,561.3. In generative workloads, small language models run at average speeds, but 70B parameter prompt processing drops to 5.88 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

With its 1:8 compute-to-memory allocation, n2-highmem-32 delivers high memory capacity without the premium cost profile of specialized multi-terabyte nodes. This footprint aligns with in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing engines, relational database services, and enterprise middleware needing substantial resident memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-32 is a memory-dense compute instance engineered for memory-heavy enterprise tasks. It provides 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 dedicated physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz, 256.0 GB of memory, and an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction support covers AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. The platform lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, depending on network storage infrastructure. Evaluated performance exhibits steady mid-tier capability across CPU and memory tests, scoring 10,454.0 on Geekbench multi-core, achieving 107.01 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, and executing 26.96 million Redis SET operations per second. While unsuited for large-scale language model inference due to weak 70B model prompt execution, its memory density provides cost-efficient operational balance for in-memory databases, large caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise services.
